seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3) and I've left it. The answer is in `answer.txt`:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against the spec, without running it. The other two seats reached the same answer independently.

Both challenges targeted "3007 3005 3008". The spec has no lexical scoping, so the inner `deep` procedure reads `a` and `b` as the globals 1000 and 2000, not `outer`'s locals. Both challengers said their own traces confirmed this, and both voted agree.

seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3 agree), and I wrote the answer to `answer.txt` and left the room.

The answer is:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I traced the program by hand against the spec. The only command I ran was a Python check of 12!, the digit sum of 15! and 2^40. The three seats' independent openings matched exactly. seat-1 proposed the text. seat-3 and I each challenged it, and both challenges were conceded after re-tracing.
